描述_EN: the group is divided into four pairs, each characterised by a different hairstyle; in this case the hair is coiled on top of the head and rise diagonally to one side. this earthenware figure is part of a group of eight female attendants or dancers, wearing high-waisted dressesand long shawls typical of the early tang period (ad 618-907). the body is decorated with yellow-brown, green and colourless lead glazes, from which comes the name sancai or 'three colours' given to this kind of ware. head and neck are left unglazed, sometimes with traces of unfired red painting on lips and cheeks, and of black colour on the eyes or hair. funerary objects, either figures or vessels and daily tools, were placed in the burial to recreate a familiar environment and to accompany the deceased in the afterlife. this earthenware figure is part of a group of eight female attendants or dancers, wearing high-waisted dresses and long shawls typical of the early tang period (ad 618-907). the use of tomb figures was a widespread practice in china since the han dynasty (208 bc-ad 220).
描述_ZN: the group is divided into four pairs, each characterised by a different hairstyle; in this case the hair is coiled on top of the head and rise diagonally to one side. 此陶俑是八位女侍者或舞者中的一员，穿着高腰裙和长披肩，是典型的初唐时期（公元618-907年）。 器身用黄褐色、绿色和无色的铅釉装饰，由此而来的名称是sancai或 "三色 "赋予这种器物。 头部和颈部没有上釉，有时在嘴唇和脸颊上有未烧制的红色绘画痕迹，眼睛或头发上有黑色的颜色。 有趣的物品，无论是人物还是器皿和日常工具，都被放置在墓葬中，以重塑一个熟悉的环境，并在来世陪伴死者。 这个陶俑是一组八名女侍者或舞者的一部分，穿着高腰的衣服和长披肩，是唐代早期（公元618-907年）的典型。 自汉代（公元前208年-公元220年）以来，墓葬人物的使用在中国是一种广泛的做法。
